title: Sustained throughput CI harness and regression detector for core model TPS/p95
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a repeatable, CI-driven harness that measures sustained tokens-per-second (TPS) and p95 latency for the set of core production models. The harness must: (1) run deterministic workloads derived from production traces with synthetic augmentation for tail lengths, (2) include warmup and cache-priming steps so measurements reflect steady-state behavior, (3) compute TPS and p95 on a per-model and per-hardware basis, and (4) publish results into Grafana and alert when regressions are detected. Deliverables: harness code in github.com/redwood-inference/tps-harness, nightly CI job, Grafana dashboard panels, and a regression detection rule document. Acceptance criteria include stable measurement variance < 3% across three runs and automatic alerting on defined regression thresholds.
tasks: Design harness architecture: runner, load generator, result aggregator
Implement production-trace ingestion + synthetic sequence generator
Add KV-cache priming and warmup phase to runner
Instrument metrics: tokens_emitted_total, requests_total, latency_histogram (for p95)
Integrate with Prometheus scrape and Grafana panels
Add regression detector: baseline storage, sliding-window compare, and anomaly thresholds
Create nightly GitHub Actions workflow and failure gating
Document runbook and add to runtime performance playbook
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Ticket created; scoped initial MVP and identified core models (redwood-7b, redwood-13b, llm-lite).
2025-11-26: Prototype runner that replays 1k trace requests with fixed batch size merged (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tps-harness/pull/12).
2025-12-10: Decided to include KV-cache priming step after comparing with production telemetry (notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Cache+Priming+Notes).
2026-01-05: Added p95 histogram buckets and validated metrics with local mock runtime. Variance across 3 runs ~4.1% for redwood-7b, working on stabilizing to <3%.
2026-02-10: Implemented baseline store in S3 + regression compare lambda; threshold defaults: 5% TPS drop OR 10% p95 increase triggers alert (RFC posted).

2026-02-28: Nightly workflow landed (https://github.com/redwood-inference/tps-harness/actions/runs/9843021); observing environment noise on hosted instances — next action: pin instance types for CI runs.
decisions: Use hybrid workload: replayed production traces (80%) + synthetic tails (20%) to exercise long-sequence code paths
Measure steady-state TPS after explicit warmup (500 requests or 60s, whichever comes first)
Baseline storage will be time-versioned in S3 with schema v1 and referenced by git tags for reproducibility
Regression thresholds initially conservative (5% TPS, 10% p95) to reduce false positives; configurable per-model
CI runs will use dedicated pinned instances rather than spot to reduce measurement variance
Use Prometheus histograms for p95 calculation and summary metric for tokens/sec to make alerts straightforward
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs in CI on each push and nightly scheduled job without flakiness > 5% failures over 10 runs
Measurement variance (TPS) < 3% across three back-to-back runs after warmup
p95 latency computed and displayed per-model; dashboard has per-run and historical comparisons
Regression detector alerts to #runtime-alerts with reproducible artifacts (logs, raw traces, diff to baseline)
Documentation and runbook complete and reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams
